title: Interfacial control of CO 2  mineralization and Ni recovery: the roles of silicate polymerization degree and nickel-bearing amount
content: Concurrent CO2 mineralization and nickel sulfidation from ultramafic rocks can present promising dual benefits to support climate resilience and the nickel (Ni) supply for the growing demand for energy security. However, the intrinsic heterogeneity of nickel content and the degree of silicate polymerization within these mineral feedstocks create complex interfacial barriers that govern reaction efficiency. A fundamental understanding of these interfacial transformations remains elusive, hindering the optimization of concurrent carbonation and sulfidation processes. To address this knowledge gap, this study investigated the carbonation and sulfidation of Ni-bearing forsterite and Ni-bearing enstatite with varying Ni concentrations under high-temperature and high-CO2-pressure conditions. The results of carbonation-only control experiments revealed that increasing Ni content reduced the extent of carbonation in both Ni-bearing forsterite and Ni-bearing enstatite. Furthermore, Ni-bearing enstatite exhibited a lower carbonation extent than Ni-bearing forsterite. This difference was attributed to the chain silicate structure of enstatite, which is more resistant to breakdown than the isolated tetrahedra structure of forsterite, causing slow dissolution and reducing carbonation. The concurrent carbonation–sulfidation results indicated that sulfidation partially decreased the extent of carbonation because Ni was converted to Ni-sulfide, which does not participate in carbonation. We found that in both minerals, the sulfidation extent decreased as the Ni content increased, and it was highest for 1.7 wt% Ni-bearing forsterite. Thus, a higher initial Ni content did not translate into a higher fractional Ni extraction by sulfidation. These findings highlight the intricate interplay between carbonation and sulfidation in ultramafic rocks and suggest that similar behaviors may occur in other ultramafic rocks with comparable structures.
